audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer says FAVOURED, difficulty 4/10, carry threat 5/10, with Mel ahead at first item and the chart only going neutral at 2+ items.
audit.why: The content layer's chart hands both first item and 2+ items to Nasus, and the matchup is 28.57%. Labelling a lane you lose from one item onward as 'favoured, 4/10' points the player at the wrong plan for the whole game.
audit.corrected: HARD, 7/10, carry threat 8/10; phases Skill / Mel x4 / Nasus / Nasus.
sources: scratchpad packet mel.json entry nasus (winRate 28.57, levelChart)

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers sell Rebuttal as a counter — the full tldr said 'you reflect what he throws', content whys[2] said 'W eats any projectile he has'. Nasus has no projectile in his kit.
audit.why: Siphoning Strike is a 255-range melee auto-reset, Wither is point-click, Spirit Fire is a ground zone and Fury of the Sands is a self-aura. Rebuttal's reflect clause has no target here, and Wither specifically cannot be dodged, blocked or returned — it has to be pre-empted with spacing.
audit.corrected: Removed the projectile claim; W is a damage blank and a speed boost in this matchup only.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json — no projectile flag on any slot

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer mentions that Fury of the Sands grants bonus attack range.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'he gains increased Health, Attack Range, damages nearby enemies, has a reduced cooldown on Siphoning Strike, and gains bonus Armor and Magic Resistance.' Against a 550-range mage with no dash the bonus attack range is the clause that actually kills — every kite distance rehearsed in lane is wrong the moment R is up, and the same button is handing him resists against your poke.
audit.corrected: Added the attack-range / armour / MR clause to phases[6].why, spikes[3].text and the content late text.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json R Fury of the Sands description

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gave no number or range for Wither, only 'bait it before you commit'.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11 at 700 range. Mel autos at 550, casts Radiant Volley at 950 and Solar Snare at 1000. The 700 figure is the entire lane: it out-reaches her auto by 150 units, so 'stay at auto range' is not safe, and its 15s downtime at rank 1 is the only window that is.
audit.corrected: Replaced with Wither's real cooldown and range plus the R timer.

audit.whatIsWrong: No layer warns against answering Nasus with raw health.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands batters nearby enemies for a share of max health, so HP items do not extend survival inside it, while the same ult hands him armour and MR against the poke you were relying on.
audit.corrected: Added to the content late text: stacking HP buys nothing against R.

edits.before: This is where the 28.57% lives. Once Nasus hits 2+ items and a big stack count, the lane is lost — his Q one-shots, R gives lifesteal and size to facetank your poke, and Wither locks you for the entire fight. Your poke can't out-damage a fed scaler and you have no dash to escape him. Your only hope is the lead you built early: end the game before ~25 minutes, group with your team, and never get caught alone where one Wither plus Q deletes your squishy frame.
edits.after: This is where the 28.57% lives. Once Nasus hits 2+ items and a big stack count, the lane is lost — Fury of the Sands adds attack range, armour and MR on a 120s cooldown, and Wither locks you for the entire fight. His R also burns a share of max health, so stacking HP does not buy you a single extra second. Your only hope is the lead you built early: end before ~25 minutes, group with your team, and never get caught alone where one Wither plus Q deletes you.
